title: Circuit breaker on sync refresh and vault init failures
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: the audited agent retried a failing sync refresh 14 times and vault init 6 times; nothing told it to stop. Change: after 2 consecutive failures of the same derived-state command with the same error signature, subsequent invocations short-circuit immediately with the existing doctor.recovery.required gap code (enforcement-gaps.ts line ~27) and a directive payload saying do-not-retry, run bwrk doctor. Breaker state persists (suggest a small runtime-state record, not a ledger event) and resets when doctor repair or a successful run of the command completes. Where: sync/vault handlers in apps/cli/src/commands.ts, gap emission via packages/core, directive text in packages/core/src/agent-directive-registry.ts. Constraint: the breaker must never block bwrk doctor itself or read-only commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Third consecutive identical sync refresh failure short-circuits with doctor.recovery.required without re-running the sync
Breaker resets after successful doctor repair or a successful manual run
doctor and read-only commands are never blocked by an open breaker
